thread:
maria: Heads-up — after the canary deploy in edge-eu1, several statefulsets that use a headless service can't reach their peers. DNS returns A records but traffic keeps going to old pod IPs. Endpoints/EndpointSlices don't seem to reflect the new pods. Anyone seen this before?

alex: Saw a similar blip in prod-edge-us this morning. Symptoms: pods report connection refused, `dig` shows both old and new IPs, kube-proxy still routes to the old ones.

maria: Quick check: `kubectl get endpointslices -n default -l kubernetes.io/service-name=my-headless -o wide` shows slices containing only the old IPs. New pods are Running with ready=true.

kevin: Could be kube-proxy not updating iptables/ipvs rules after EndpointSlice updates. Which kube-proxy mode are you on (iptables vs ipvs)? Also check conntrack entries — stale conntrack can keep flows pinned.

jamal: Ran a couple of commands from a broken pod: `dig my-headless.default.svc.cluster.local +short` -> returns mixed IPs; `kubectl get endpoints my-headless -o yaml` shows no endpoints for the new pods.

infra-bot: [alert] EndpointController: reconcile delay > 30s on node edge-12 (detected at 2025-09-02T08:23:14Z)

alex: Commands I ran: 
- `kubectl get endpoints -n default my-headless -o yaml` -> empty subsets
- `kubectl get endpointslices -n default -l kubernetes.io/service-name=my-headless -o yaml` -> slices with only old IPs
- checked kube-proxy metrics on node: `curl -s localhost:10249/metrics | grep sync` shows recent sync but no endpoint updates count increment

maria: Workaround that fixed traffic immediately: `kubectl delete pod -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-proxy --field-selector spec.nodeName=edge-12` to restart kube-proxy on the affected node. Traffic started routing to the new pods after restart. Not a long-term fix though.

kevin: Two leading theories: 1) kube-proxy watch for EndpointSlice is flapping / being throttled and misses updates (so local rules aren't updated). 2) conntrack exhaustion keeps old flows alive and requests keep getting DNAT'd. Check `conntrack -L | wc -l` and `kubectl logs -n kube-system kube-proxy-<pod> | tail -n200` for watch errors/throttling.

jamal: I pulled apiserver audit logs for the edge-eu1 nodes and see a lot of `429 Too Many Requests` on watch requests originating from kube-proxy service account around the time of deploy. Looks like API server burst limit hit for those nodes.

maria: That explains it — kube-proxy loses the EndpointSlice watch and doesn't reconcile until restart. Proposal: increase API server burst/qps for kube-proxy SA (or the kubelet/kube-proxy client config) on edge clusters and bump kube-proxy to the patch that fixes EndpointSlice watch resilience. Also add a readiness/liveness probe to restart kube-proxy when watch disconnects persist.

alex: Agreed. Plan:
- immediate: restart kube-proxy on the 3 most affected nodes (edge-12/edge-14/edge-19) to restore traffic
- short term: raise client QPS/Burst for kube-proxy from 10/20 -> 50/100 on edge clusters
- medium: rollout kube-proxy patched image that has EndpointSlice watch backoff improvements
- monitor: add an alert for kube-proxy watch disconnects and a metric for EndpointSlice-applied count

kevin: Also increase `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` if conntrack counts are near the limit on those nodes. Run `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` and `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max`. If >80% usage, bump it and restart.

maria: Quick commands I'm pasting here: 
```
# check EndpointSlices for service
kubectl get endpointslices -n default -l kubernetes.io/service-name=my-headless -o wide

# restart kube-proxy on a specific node
kubectl delete pod -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-proxy --field-selector spec.nodeName=edge-12

# conntrack checks (on node)
sudo conntrack -L | wc -l
cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
```

jamal: I'll own the ticket, will raise the kube-proxy client QPS/Burst change, schedule restarts on the three nodes during the next 15m maintenance window, and follow up with upgrade plan.

alex: :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks everyone — let's keep this thread updated with the ticket number and postmortem once we confirm root cause and fix.
